turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Hi Dev. I am Wren, and I am glad you are here. How are you feeling about starting out today?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey Wren. A little nervous, to be honest. I taught high school math for seven years, but I'm trying to make the jump into data analyst work now.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Seven years in the classroom is serious work. What made you want to move toward data?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I guess I've always loved digging into numbers and finding patterns, not just teaching formulas. So over the past year, I've been teaching myself SQL and Python after school.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That takes real discipline after a full day of teaching. Did you get to work with data much in your school role?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yeah, actually. I built a grading dashboard in Excel that tracked quiz scores for a hundred and twenty students, and it flagged whoever was falling behind. It was kind of my first taste of real analytics.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: That is a real data project. How did you use those flags during the term?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It let me pull kids aside for extra review before unit exams instead of waiting until report cards came out. Parents really appreciated it too, honestly.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: You solved a clear problem with data. Does framing your classroom projects as analyst experience feel strange to you?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A bit, yeah. I worry hiring managers will just look at my resume and think, oh, he's just a teacher, not a real data person.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: Teaching involves communication and problem solving, which analysts need every day. What parts of the transition feel the toughest right now?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mostly just translating what I did into interview answers that sound crisp. I tend to wander off into teaching anecdotes if I'm not careful.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: We will practice keeping your answers tight and focused. Would you like to map out a few core stories next time?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That sounds like a great plan. I think that Excel dashboard story could be a solid starting point.

turns.speaker: wren
turns.text: It definitely has teeth. How are your energy levels holding up after today's chat?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Pretty good! It's just nice to know I don't have to figure all this interview prep out alone.
